description: Apply authoritative Slack Bot-message admission across the adapter, Agent Connection ingress, and Mohist App Manager ingress without durable or user-facing side effects.

tasks.title: Propagate sender classification and Bot author identity through adapter transports
tasks.description: Make Slack adapter normalization the source of truth for the lower-case human, bot, and unknown sender classifications, with Bot markers taking precedence over a supplied user ID. Preserve optional managed-Bot author App metadata separately from the receiving apiAppId, carry both fields in the complete Connection envelope and the reduced Manager transport envelope, and make Socket Mode treat a successful ignored result as an acknowledged, non-user-facing delivery. Add adapter normalization, event-flow, author-identity, and transport serialization regression coverage.
acceptanceCriteria: `normalizeSocketEvent` classifies events with `bot_id` or `subtype = bot_message` as `bot` even when `user` is present, classifies a non-empty user without Bot markers as `human`, and classifies missing user and missing Bot markers as `unknown` with `senderSlackUserId = null`.

Every normalized Slack text envelope includes `senderKind`; Bot envelopes also preserve the optional author App identity extracted from Slack Bot metadata, without confusing it with the receiving `apiAppId`. Connection requests retain these fields unchanged, and Manager transport requests include the same values while retaining a null sender ID for a Bot event without `user`.

When target ingress returns `{ kind: "ignored" }`, `SlackAdapter.handleEvent` acknowledges the Socket Mode event and emits no Web-client rejection or acknowledgement; transport and Server failures retain the existing unacknowledged behavior.

Adapter tests cover a Mohist Manager App Bot without `user` and with author App metadata, a Mohist Agent App Bot including another Bot's message, a third-party Bot classification, human classification, explicit unknown classification, ignored-result acknowledgement, and no user-facing Slack post.
Transport tests assert the serialized Manager request body preserves the source envelope's `senderKind`, and the focused Slack adapter test suite passes.
tasks.output: Updated Slack adapter normalization, envelope/transport contracts, Socket acknowledgement flow, and passing adapter and transport regression tests.
tasks.notes: Keep the wire values exactly `human`, `bot`, and `unknown`. Preserve author App metadata separately from the receiving `apiAppId`; do not locally drop Bot events before Server admission. The Server contract and adapter should be released together.

tasks.title: Ignore managed Bot events before Agent Connection work admission
tasks.description: Add a Server-side managed-Bot identity resolver that reads the active Mohist Manager and identity-bound Agent App identities for the message workspace. At the Agent Connection ingress boundary, admit a Bot-classified event as ignored immediately after operator authentication, lease validation, stable message identity validation, and the read-only managed-identity check only when its author App or supplied Bot user identity matches that set. Return before disabled-Connection auditing, owner or access checks, routing, claim handling, session lookup, attachment binding, inbox admission, and outbox creation. Unmatched third-party Bot events must fall through the existing Connection behavior; human and unknown-sender behavior remains unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: A valid Mohist-managed Bot-classified channel mention or DM returns `{ kind: "ignored" }` without requiring a human sender ID and without evaluating owner/access policy, channel or DM routing, claims, session state, attachments, or durable input admission.

A Mohist-managed Bot event received for a disabled Connection is ignored before disabled-event auditing, and a managed-Bot follow-up in an already-bound thread or existing DM session leaves session mappings, SessionInput history, pending outbox state, and all other baseline work state unchanged.

Agent Connection ingress creates no provider inbox row, SessionInput, AgentJob, Agent Session, follow-up, thread or DM binding, disabled-discarded audit row, outbox row, or user-facing Slack response for an ignored Bot event; a unique sentinel message is not persisted or logged as work input.

Existing human channel mentions, DMs, and bound-thread follow-ups retain their current authorization and routing behavior; explicit `unknown` events retain their current ignored or rejected non-work behavior and are not promoted to human; and an unmatched third-party Bot follows the pre-616 Connection behavior, including disabled-event handling where that path previously applied.

Focused Agent Connection specs cover an managed Agent App Bot mention from another Mohist-managed Bot, a managed Bot DM,  a disabled Connection, a bound-thread or existing-session follow-up, an unmatched third-party Bot regression, no-side-effects assertions, and human/unknown regression cases; the Slack Server test suite passes.
tasks.output: Updated Agent Connection Slack ingress with early Bot admission and passing ingress, disabled-Connection, follow-up, human, unknown, and no-side-effects regression tests.
tasks.notes: Resolve managed identities read-only from existing workspace enrollment and ManagedSlackAgentApp records; no schema change is needed. Keep the managed-Bot guard before disabled-Connection auditing and every operation that can mutate work state. Unmatched third-party Bots must use the existing path. A managed Bot still passes transport authentication, lease validation, and stable message identity validation.

tasks.title: Ignore managed Manager Bot events before actor and conversation admission
tasks.description: Carry sender classification and Bot author metadata through the Manager HTTP route and ingress service. After transport authentication, lease validation, stable identity validation, and the read-only managed-identity check, a valid Mohist-managed Bot-classified direct message without `senderSlackUserId` returns ignored before Manager actor authentication, enrollment or access checks, claim consumption, inbox admission, session processing, and outbox delivery. Preserve explicit unknown semantics and the existing Manager behavior for unmatched third-party Bots and human messages, with focused no-side-effects coverage.
acceptanceCriteria: The Manager route does not reject a valid Mohist-managed Bot-classified message merely because `senderSlackUserId` is absent; after transport authentication, lease validation, stable identity validation, and managed-identity resolution it returns an ignored result without authenticating a Manager actor or consuming a claim.

Managed Manager Bot admission occurs before enrollment or access authorization, actor lookup, claim handling, conversation or session processing, provider inbox insertion, SessionInput, AgentJob, Agent Session, follow-up, session mapping, or outbox creation, and `SlackManagerIngressResult.Ignored()` contains no inbox identifier or delivery-intent flag.

A Mohist Manager App Bot message with a unique sentinel text creates no inbox or work records and does not persist or log the text as work input; it produces no user-facing Slack response, while repeated delivery remains harmless.

Human Manager messages with `senderKind = human` retain existing claim, authorization, conversation, SessionInput, and response-delivery behavior; explicit `unknown` messages retain their existing non-human rejection or ignore behavior rather than being inferred as human from an ID; and an unmatched third-party Bot retains the existing Manager sender validation and authorization behavior.

Focused Manager route and service specs cover a Mohist Manager App Bot direct message without sender ID, explicit unknown handling, human routing, an unmatched third-party Bot regression, no actor or claim interaction, no-side-effects assertions, and the ignored result shape; the Slack Server test suite passes.
tasks.output: Updated Manager Slack ingress contract, route, and service with early Bot admission plus passing Manager ingress and no-side-effects regression tests.
tasks.notes: Use the shared Server-side managed-Bot identity resolver and sender-kind parser to keep route semantics identical. Any compatibility fallback for omitted senderKind must never override an explicit `unknown` value, and an unmatched `bot` classification must not enter the new ignored branch.
